title: Getting a CPH number and registering a holding
subtitle: The first step before keeping any farm livestock in the UK.
excerpt: A County Parish Holding (CPH) number is the unique identifier for land used to keep farm livestock in the UK. It is required before you can register animals, apply for livestock passports, or move animals onto or off your land. Registration is free and takes 10 to 15 minutes to apply for online. Here is what the process involves and what happens after registration.
sourceNotes: Rural Payments Agency, CPH registration guidance (2023). DEFRA, Livestock identification and traceability guidance. APHA, new keeper information.

glossaryTerms.definition: County Parish Holding number. A nine-digit number in the format county code / parish code / holding number (e.g. 11/222/3333). Assigned to a piece of land, not to a person. Required to register livestock or apply for payments on that land.

Animal and Plant Health Agency. The government body responsible for animal disease control, livestock traceability, and import/export health checks in England and Wales. Equivalent bodies in Scotland (SGRPID) and Northern Ireland (DAERA).

content.text: is registered to a piece of land, not to a person. If you move to a new holding, you apply for a new CPH for that land. The same person can hold multiple CPH numbers if they keep livestock on more than one site.

Poultry and rabbits kept for personal use do not need a CPH in most UK nations. Keepers of flocks over 50 birds must register separately with
A CPH is required before you can receive RPA payments (such as BPS or ELMS) on that land.

In England: apply online through the Rural Payments service at ruralpayments.service.gov.uk. You will need a single business identifier (SBI) number first; this is created as part of the same registration.
In Wales: apply through the RPW Online portal.
In Scotland: apply through the Scottish Government's rural payments service.
You will need the OS grid reference or postcode of the land, the area in hectares, and your personal details. You do not need to own the land; a lease or grazing agreement is sufficient.
Register with BCMS (British Cattle Movement Service) if keeping cattle: bcms.gov.uk. This links your CPH number to the cattle traceability database.
Register your flock with APHA if keeping sheep or goats: a flock number is issued and attached to your CPH.
Register your herd mark with the local authority if keeping pigs. This is different from the CPH and is the mark applied to pig identification before movement.
Set up your holding register once registrations are complete. You must begin recording animal movements from the day your first animal arrives.
